key_facts: NOV reported first-quarter 2021 revenues of $1.25 billion and a net loss of $115 million.
The first quarter was affected by severe winter weather in Texas and Oklahoma, shutting down 63 NOV facilities for a week or more.
New pandemic control measures shut down additional large plants and disrupted supply chains for raw materials like fiberglass and resin.
Higher costs from poor execution on two projects impacted the first-quarter results.
Despite challenges, results slightly exceeded the March forecast due to cost reductions and early signs of recovery in the oil field, especially in Wellbore Technologies and North America.
North American oilfield activity showed recovery during the quarter, with March revenues up sharply from January for some businesses.
International markets also began showing early signs of recovery.
Consolidated revenue declined 6% sequentially due to the backlog pummeling in 2020.
EBITDA fell to breakeven, prompting further cost reductions.
Oil prices went negative in April 2020, and U.S. rig count hit its lowest level since records began in World War II in August 2020.
North American frac fleet utilization dropped to single digits.
Over 100 North American oil and gas companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection by year-end 2020 with combined debt exceeding $100 billion.
FIDs (Final Investment Decisions) for offshore projects in 2020 would have been the lowest since 1960 without a few large pre-lockdown projects.
Average first quarter 2021 rig counts were down 46% for North America land, 36% for international land, and 31% for offshore compared to the previous year.
NOV’s oilfield backlogs decreased throughout 2020, with the first-quarter annualized revenue run rate down 45% from five quarters ago.
Historically, the current downturn is considered the worst in the industry.
Idled equipment became a competitor as utilization collapsed and service companies struggled to stay operational.
Day rates in 2020 reached desperate levels as companies discounted to keep assets and crews working.
NOV has cut costs by $12.6 billion since 2014, including $2 billion annually in fixed cost reductions.
NOV used $27 million in cash during Q1 2021, with capital expenditures totaling $49 million.
NOV ended Q1 2021 with $1.61 billion in cash and $1.85 billion in gross debt, resulting in net debt of $244 million.
NOV redeemed $183 million in senior notes due in December 2022, pushing its next bond maturity to December 2029.
Interest expense is expected to decline roughly $1 million per quarter following the redemption.
Wellbore Technologies generated $413 million in revenue during Q1 2021, an 11% sequential increase.
ReedHycalog drill bit business saw 20% revenue growth, driven by market share gains and improved pricing.
Downhole Tool business experienced a 13% sequential improvement in revenue.
WellSite Services recorded a 16% sequential revenue increase, primarily from solid control operations.
M/D Totco achieved low single-digit revenue growth, with record rental service revenue from eVolve wire drill pipe optimization services.
Tuboscope pipe coating and inspection business posted a 10% sequential revenue increase, with demand particularly strong in the U.S.
Grant Prideco drill pipe business had a high single-digit sequential revenue increase, with a book-to-bill ratio of 104%.
Completion & Production Solutions segment generated $439 million in revenue during Q1 2021, a 20% sequential decrease.
The segment's book-to-bill ratio was 127%, its first above 100% since Q4 2019.
Fiber Glass Systems business realized a 25% sequential revenue decline due to absorption challenges and supply chain issues.
Intervention & Stimulation Equipment business experienced a mid-single-digit sequential decline but achieved a book-to-bill greater than 1 for the second consecutive quarter.
Cementing equipment orders doubled from the second half of 2020, indicating growing demand.
XL Systems conductor pipe business faced a sharp sequential revenue decline but achieved a 143% book-to-bill ratio.
Subsea flexible pipe business saw a low double-digit sequential revenue decline with outsized decremental margins.
Rig Technologies segment generated $431 million in revenue during Q1 2021, a 1% sequential decrease.
Segment book-to-bill ratio was 59%, with weak orders for rig capital equipment despite improved quotation levels.
NOV started manufacturing the first two rigs at its new plant in Saudi Arabia, with delivery expected by year-end 2021.
The Saudi plant has a commitment for 50 drilling rigs over the next 10 years and $1.8 billion in backlog.
Renewables business booked an order for design, jacking systems, and crane for a European wind turbine installation vessel.
NOV expects modest offshore wind order intake in Q1 but pursues over $400 million in potential projects before year-end.
